transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-22
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (AsterHealth Head of ML), Marcus Lee (AsterHealth CTO), Sara Kim (AsterHealth Procurement), Ethan Park (Data Eng)
Shared artifacts: Pilot term sheet (Redwood): https://redwood.app/pilot-term-sheet, Benchmark harness (to be shared), Security binder link noted in chat

Summary (auto): discuss pilot credits, guardrails, go/no-go metrics, logistics for benchmark run, procurement pathway for moving from pilot to committed reserved capacity.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and daniel's our SE. Quick intros?
[00:12] Priya Singh: Hey I'm Priya, head of ML at AsterHealth, leading this pilot. Marcus and Sara are on to help with infra and procurement.
[00:20] Marcus Lee: Marcus, CTO. We'll be watching latency and with a close eye to cost.
[00:25] Sara Kim: Sara, procurement. I'll flag any must-haves for terms.
[00:30] Daniel Ortiz: Hi all, Daniel - I'll own the benchmark and technical run.

[02:00] Maya Chen: High level agenda — we want to align on the POC objectives, the workload size you expect, the benchmarks we'll run, and importantly commercial guardrails: how we cap pilot spend, what credits look like, and what the procurement path is afterwards.
[02:22] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Our immediate goal is to validate we can hit latency and throughput targets for our patient-facing summarization pipeline and an entity extraction endpoint. We have mixed lengths — avg 400 tokens, some up to 1,200. Typical concurrency is 15-30 simultaneous users, peak egress ~60 qps in peak 10-minute windows.
[03:05] Daniel Ortiz: Good — that gives us a shape. For benchmarking we'll run a synthetic replay of your traces plus a subset of real prompts. Can you confirm average tokens/request and QPS?
[03:18] Priya Singh: average ~400 tokens/request, about 20 qps sustained, peaks 60 qps for <15 min. We can generate trace files for you.
[03:30] Maya Chen: Perfect. On the commercial side we typically do a 2-week pilot for this class of workload with capped credits. For clarity: pilot credits will be applied to a hosted trial account; if you need private/VPC we can do a short-term dedicated evaluation but that usually takes longer.
[03:52] Marcus Lee: When you say credits, is that a hard cap or just an offset? We need guardrails so we don't surprise finance.
[04:00] Maya Chen: It's a hard cap for the pilot. We'll issue a coupon-like credit that stops serving once exhausted, or we'll notify and pause — whichever you prefer. We can also configure an alert at 75% consumption.
[04:15] Sara Kim: From procurement, we prefer a short SOW that references the pilot and a simple PO that covers the pilot credits. Any long-form T&Cs required?
[04:26] Maya Chen: For pilots we use a lightweight pilot SOW plus our standard trial terms. If you need specific security or indemnity language, we can escalate but for the initial pilot most customers accept the pilot SOW and then discuss enterprise terms if moving to production.
[04:40] Sara Kim: What about data residency and logs? We need audit logs retained for six months.
[04:46] Daniel Ortiz: We can enable longer retention on request for the pilot, though for private deployments we support direct storage in your VPC and KMS; for hosted we provide encrypted logs with configurable retention. We'll include the retention in the term sheet.

[06:00] Priya Singh: Let's talk success criteria. We're proposing: 1) Latency p50 < 300ms, p95 < 800ms on the summarization path for avg 400 tokens, 2) Entity extraction F1 > 0.90 on our benchmark set, and 3) Throughput 20 qps sustained with acceptable error rates (<1%). If Redwood can meet that under hosted pilot conditions we consider pilot a pass.
[06:29] Daniel Ortiz: Those are measurable. For latencies, we need to specify model family and context lengths. We'll run with a small/wide variant first — quantized if helpful — to match cost goals. We'll capture end-to-end times including network.
[06:48] Maya Chen: Important note — hosted inference includes multiple model variants. For cost reasons we can test a 7B quantized variant as a baseline, and if you want lower latency we can test a 13B or more at the end. For the pilot credits we'll outline which model SKUs are included so there's no surprise.
[07:10] Marcus Lee: Will the pilot cap cover the larger models or only baseline? We need to know if testing 13B will burn through credits quickly.
[07:17] Maya Chen: We'll list included SKUs in the term sheet. If you want a stretch run on a 13B we can either allot separate credits or bill overage with pre-approval.

[08:30] Sara Kim: How do we transition to procurement for production? If pilot succeeds, we want an outline: SOW, pricing for dedicated vs hosted, expected committed spend, and procurement timelines.
[08:45] Maya Chen: Typical path: pilot SOW + PO for credits (2 weeks). If pilot successful: Redwood drafts an enterprise SOW + an offer for Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private deployment pricing. That usually requires legal review and can take 30-60 days depending on your process. We can provide an expedited playbook for customers with faster procurement.
[09:10] Sara Kim: And billing — monthly invoice or annual commit?
[09:14] Maya Chen: For Dedicated we do reserved capacity with monthly or annual billing; for hosted customers often prefer monthly usage billing. We'll include options in the follow-up.

[10:20] Daniel Ortiz: Back to benchmarks — we'll need sample payloads, request traces, and an SLO matrix. Priya, can you share three representative prompt sets: short summarization, long-form summarization, and entity extraction?
[10:33] Priya Singh: Yes, we'll share that by Thursday. We'll also include the trace file with timestamps so you can replay real traffic.
[10:40] Daniel Ortiz: Great. We'll also share a benchmark harness — it's a small script that replays traces, measures p50/p95, token cost, and error rates. For accuracy we'll run your labeled set and compute F1 for entity extraction.

[12:00] Marcus Lee: On security, we need SOC 2 and ISO references. For private deployment we need KMS integration.
[12:08] Maya Chen: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO coverage — we'll attach the security binder. KMS and customer-managed keys are available in Private deployments; hosted has encryption-at-rest with Redwood-managed keys unless you opt for bring-your-own-key in certain regions.

[14:00] Sara Kim: What's the approval workflow for any overage during the pilot? We cannot accept surprise charges.
[14:07] Maya Chen: We'll disable auto-billing for pilots by default — it's credit capped. Any proposed overage would require written approval from your procurement contact. We can also set a hard stop.

[16:20] Priya Singh: Timeline-wise, we propose: share artifacts this week, run benchmarks next week (2-3 days to run), evaluation period the week after, final decision within two weeks of pilot end. That puts full decision in ~5-6 weeks if everything goes smoothly.
[16:40] Daniel Ortiz: That aligns. We can compress benchmark runs into a 48-hour window if you provide a test account and traces.

[18:00] Ethan Park: Small infra note — we'll want a service account and restricted credentials that expire with pilot. Can you provide that?
[18:07] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, we'll create a scoped API key for the pilot that you can rotate or expire. We'll provide instructions in the onboarding doc.

[20:00] Marcus Lee: For the benchmark, will you simulate network latency from our region? We need realistic numbers for end-to-end.
[20:08] Daniel Ortiz: We can run from a region close to your app or inject network latency in the harness. Let us know which region you consider primary.
[20:20] Priya Singh: US-west for us.

[22:00] Maya Chen: Commercial guardrails recap: 2-week pilot, hard credit cap applied to hosted account, SKUs listed in term sheet, alerting at 75% consumption, no auto-billing, overage only with written approval, security binder to be shared, and procurement path clarified (pilot PO then enterprise SOW). Any objections?
[22:25] Sara Kim: That sounds fine. We'll need the term sheet to reflect PO billing info and any minimum insurance/indemnity clauses — I'll mark items in the doc.
[22:35] Maya Chen: Understood — we'll include placeholders for insurance and standard indemnity language and escalate if your legal team needs changes.

[24:00] Priya Singh: Metrics for go/no-go: latency p50/p95 thresholds, F1 score, error rate <1%, and cost per 1k tokens below a threshold. We'll define exact numbers in the success criteria doc.
[24:18] Daniel Ortiz: We'll instrument token accounting and produce a cost per request breakdown in the benchmark report.

[26:00] Maya Chen: Notes on pilot SKUs and quantization: quantized 7B models usually give the best cost/latency trade-off for 400-token payloads. If you need to test longer sequences up to 1,200 tokens we'll include a couple of runs to validate memory and latency.
[26:30] Marcus Lee: Please list the expected token pricing per SKU in the term sheet so we can model cost.
[26:37] Maya Chen: Will do. We'll also provide recommended batching and prefix cache settings — though prefix caching may be less effective for high variance prompts.

[29:00] Priya Singh: One potential blocker: PHI concerns. Are there specific notes you need about de-identification or on-prem requirement?
[29:12] Daniel Ortiz: If PHI is required, we recommend Private deployment or strict data handling controls. For hosted pilots we can sign a data processing addendum and enforce retention rules; for production you may prefer VPC/private.
[29:30] Priya Singh: We'll flag which datasets are de-identified for the pilot.

[32:00] Sara Kim: Procurement question: can the pilot PO be net-30? We need to align with our payment terms.
[32:08] Maya Chen: Net-30 is standard for pilot POs for many customers. We'll note that in the term sheet — if your legal needs further custom payment terms we'll handle in the enterprise SOW.

[34:00] Daniel Ortiz: Technical deliverables: benchmark harness, measuring p50/p95, token cost, error rates, F1 report for extraction. We'll also include a runbook for onboarding.

[36:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap and owners — action items I've noted. We'll share the pilot-term-sheet PDF, the benchmark harness repo link, and a checklist for the pilot onboarding.
[36:20] Priya Singh: Good. One ask: can Redwood provide a short cost estimate for running the same workload at 20 qps sustained for a month as an apples-to-apples compare? That will help budgeting if we go production.
[36:35] Maya Chen: Yes — we'll include an estimated monthly spend for hosted and a committed reserved capacity quote for Dedicated.

[38:00] Marcus Lee: Any mention of competitor differences — latency trade-offs vs Anthropic we discussed?
[38:08] Daniel Ortiz: We won't replicate exact competitor claims, but our benchmark will be reproducible and you can run it side-by-side. We noted Anthropic and OpenAI as comparators.

[40:00] Sara Kim: Please add contacts for legal and security review on the term sheet so we have direct people to escalate to.
[40:10] Maya Chen: We'll add our security and legal contacts in the doc and a short FAQ for procurement.

[42:00] Priya Singh: Any limitations on model outputs for this pilot? e.g., rate limits or content policy?
[42:10] Daniel Ortiz: Standard content policy applies. For high-volume or regulated content we'll document policy exceptions and routing to private deployments.

[44:00] Maya Chen: OK we'll wrap with the formal next steps: Maya to send pilot-term-sheet and pricing by Friday 2025-04-25; Daniel to share benchmark harness and sample payloads by Thursday 2025-04-24; Priya to share traces and labeled eval data by 2025-04-24; Sara to confirm PO timeline and any legal must-haves by 2025-05-02.
[44:40] Sara Kim: That timeline works.

[46:00] Ethan Park: I'll provision test accounts and get creds to Daniel once we have the onboarding doc.
[46:10] Daniel Ortiz: Thanks Ethan. We'll keep keys scoped and short-lived.

[48:00] Maya Chen: Any final questions?
[48:05] Marcus Lee: None here.
[48:10] Priya Singh: Thanks — excited to run the benchmarks.
[48:15] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up in email with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the benchmark window. Thanks everyone.
